questions.question: What is wave interference?
choices: A wave changing direction at a boundary
The combination of overlapping wave displacements
A wave changing speed between media
The regular change in a source's frequency

questions.question: What is constructive interference?
choices: Opposite displacements cancel at overlap
A wave bends when entering a different medium
Overlapping displacements reinforce each other
A wave's frequency increases at every overlap

questions.question: What is destructive interference?
choices: Two displacements reinforce at overlap
A wave reflects from a fixed boundary
A wave's speed decreases during every overlap
Opposite displacements partly or completely cancel at overlap

questions.question: What is a node in a standing wave?
choices: A point with maximum displacement amplitude
The highest-frequency wave in a group
A point with zero displacement amplitude
The source of every reflected wave

questions.question: What is an antinode in a standing wave?
choices: A point with maximum displacement amplitude
A point that never oscillates
A point outside the wave's medium
A point with zero wavelength

questions.question: What is resonance?
choices: The absence of all oscillation
A strong response when driving frequency is near a system's natural frequency
A permanent decrease in mass
A change from sound into electric charge

questions.question: What does damping do to a freely oscillating system?
choices: Increases amplitude continuously without energy input
Necessarily raises the natural frequency to infinity
Reduces oscillation amplitude over time
Keeps amplitude fixed regardless of energy loss

questions.question: Why can two overlapping pulses cancel briefly without being permanently destroyed?
choices: The pulses reflect from each other instead of passing through
Each pulse continues propagating after the overlap
The medium loses the energy of both pulses permanently
The two pulses must stop at the overlap

questions.question: Why can identical sound waves produce different loudness at different locations?
choices: Sound amplitude must be equal at every location
Every point receives the same phase relationship
Sound frequency alone determines the interference pattern
Their relative phase can vary with path length

questions.question: How does increasing damping usually affect a resonant response?
choices: It reduces the sharpness and amplitude of the response
It increases the resonant amplitude without additional input
It eliminates all possible motion of the system
It makes the driving force create energy

questions.question: What produces a standing wave on a string?
choices: Interference between waves traveling in opposite directions
Interference between equal waves moving only in one direction
Movement of the string as a whole without oscillation
A source whose frequency changes randomly each instant

questions.question: Why can an oscillating system respond strongly to a small periodic force?
choices: Small periodic forces supply no energy to the system
Natural frequency depends only on the applied force's magnitude
Repeated pushes at a suitable frequency add energy effectively
Every push gives an equally strong response at every timing

questions.question: Why is complete destructive interference possible at a point for two waves?
choices: Their speeds must both be zero
Their displacements can be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction
Their wavelengths must be zero
Their media must be different

questions.question: Why does a node remain still while nearby parts of a standing-wave string move?
choices: The string material is absent at each node
The string moves at maximum amplitude at a node
Both traveling waves have zero amplitude everywhere
Oppositely traveling wave displacements cancel there

questions.question: What causes beats when two similar sound frequencies overlap?
choices: A steady change in the speed of sound
Alternating reinforcement and cancellation
Permanent elimination of one of the two tones
Equal reinforcement at every instant

questions.question: At an instant, two upward pulses have displacements of 2 cm and 3 cm at the same point. What is the combined displacement?
choices: 5 cm upward
1 cm upward
6 cm upward
0 cm

questions.question: At an instant, a +3 cm displacement overlaps a −3 cm displacement. What is the resultant displacement?
choices: +6 cm
−6 cm
0 cm
+3 cm

questions.question: Two tones have frequencies of 250 Hz and 254 Hz. What is the beat frequency?
choices: 504 Hz
252 Hz
4 Hz

questions.question: A swing has a natural period of 2 seconds. Which regular push timing best supports resonance?
choices: One suitably timed push every 2 seconds
One push every 0.1 second regardless of position
Randomly timed pushes
One push followed by no further pushes

questions.question: A string fixed at both ends forms its fundamental standing wave. Where is its displacement antinode?
choices: At either fixed end
At every point equally
Only beyond the string
At the midpoint
